subject: Regional alliance: local deployment guardrails and SI responsibilities
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@astratech.com>; ops@kumo-systems.io
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Regional alliance: local deployment guardrails and SI responsibilities

Hi Sara / Kumo ops team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — appreciate the thoughtful questions on our private deployment model. Per follow-up, I wanted to capture a concise set of guardrails we need to finalize before we proceed to an SI-led pilot in IE/DE/APAC regions:  

- Data residency: customer datasets must remain in-region (Ireland/Germany/APAC region) unless explicit export consent is documented.
- Control plane: we support private control plane with customer-managed VPC. For EU customers we prefer the control plane to be hosted inside an EU region.
- Key management: Redwood supports KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys. For any local SI-managed deployments we need a binding KMS policy and proof of HSM (if requested by the customer).
- Audit & evidence: SOC2 + runtime audit logs are required; we will provide a retention snapshot for the pilot (30 days) and can extend per contract.
- SI responsibilities: infra provisioning, local networking, and escalation path to Redwood runtime team. Redwood owns model rollouts, model cataloging, and backplane updates.

Attached: a first-draft MOU and an SI deployment checklist to map specific handoffs.

Next steps I propose:
1) Sara + Kumo confirm which EU/APAC locations they plan to host and any preferred KMS vendor (Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS, Thales/HSM).
2) Marissa to scope commercial terms for a pilot (60-day pilot + optional retainer).
3) Technical deep-dive with Hiro to walk through HSM integration and the private control plane network diagram (propose week of Nov 17).

If that looks right, I'll draft a short mutual action plan and circulate.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise GTM | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0189

--

Subject: Re: Regional alliance: local deployment guardrails and SI responsibilities

Jordan — thanks for the summary, this is helpful. A few flags from AstraTech's side:  

- For our EU customers in Germany we have a standing requirement for HSM-backed key storage or a validated Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) flow. Will Redwood's private control plane support customer-managed HSMs via standard PKCS#11 interfaces?
- On data export: we can allow aggregated telemetry to leave region but PII/data subject records must never be exported without signed consent and a legal addendum.
- For APAC pilots (SG / JP) we may have an additional data localization clause required by a couple of customers; we'll need the SI to demonstrate network segmentation and route restrictions.

Kumo — can you confirm the SI's prior experience with HSMs and whether you have a preferred KMS vendor?

Looking forward to Marissa's commercial framework.

—Sara
Head of Integrations, AstraTech
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 08 Nov 2025 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Regional alliance: local deployment guardrails and SI responsibilities

Forwarding Sara's note — flagged for commercial.

Jordan / team: draft commercial outline below (high level):

- Pilot structure: 60-day pilot, up to 5 nodes in-region, capped tokens throughput 5M tokens/month.
- Fees: one-time pilot setup $15k (covers network, baseline integration), month-to-month pilot fee $12k (covers reserved capacity + support).
- Security add-ons: HSM integration + documented KMS attestation = one-time $6k engineering onboarding; ongoing HSM management + logs retention surcharge = $2k/mo.
- SLA / liability: standard pilot excludes SLA credits; production rollouts will include a 99.9% uptime target with commercial SLA.

Action: I'll convert this into a short MOU and route it to AstraTech + Kumo for signature. Please confirm if we should include a limited export consent template (yes/no).

Marissa Cole
Sr. Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@astratech.com>; Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 02:15:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Regional alliance: local deployment guardrails and SI responsibilities

Sara — quick technical clarifications (cc Jordan / Marissa):

On HSM / KMS:
- Redwood runtime supports KMIP and PKCS#11 via an HSM gateway for private control plane deployments. We also support cloud KMS providers (Azure, GCP, AWS) with customer-managed keys; BYOK flows are supported with our key-rotation hooks.
- For customers requiring FIPS-140 Level 3 HSMs we will require an architecture review and a short validation run (typically 2-3 weeks) to validate TLS termination and key provisioning flows.

On data residency / export controls:
- We can configure token-level masking and a TTL-based KV cache that ensures no persistent PII is written to any long-term store outside the region. Runtime logs can be routed to a local SI-managed ELK/Splunk instance.

On SI responsibilities:
- Kumo must provide the network peering config, firewall rules, and a jumpbox for our runtime engineers to run the validation checklist.
- We'll provide a hardened AMI/container image and an ops runbook. The SI will perform initial infra provisioning and the smoke tests; Redwood will triage runtime issues during the pilot.

On quoting: add the 2-3 week validation for FIPS/HSM as a separate line item in the SOW.

Thanks,
Hiro Tanaka
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
